ravi (encops): Quick alert from the nightly backup validator: ~12 objects across prod and staging show `head-object` with no SSE headers. Sizes match expected snapshots. Likely around the infra permission boundary change yesterday.

leah (infra-oncall): Which principal did the uploads use? We rolled out a permission boundary to service roles at 03:00UTC. Could block kms:GenerateDataKey.

dan (backup-service): Uploads from `backup-uploader` service account at 02:45-03:10UTC. Our client logs show failures on GenerateDataKey but uploader proceeded to PutObject without encryption header (library fallback). Snippet: `GenerateDataKey failed: AccessDenied` then `PutObject ok`.

ravi (encops): Confirmed in CloudTrail: PutObject requestParameters.headers empty for the affected keys. Also a flurry of GenerateDataKey AccessDenied entries matching the window.

leah (infra-oncall): Looks like the permission boundary removed kms:* from the role temporarily. That explains it. Immediate mitigation: block PutObject from that principal to backups bucket so we don't get more plaintext snapshots. I'll push a quick deny policy.

dan (backup-service): Pausing uploads now. I can queue a rewrite job to re-upload affected objects once we restore KMS rights. How many objects?

ravi (encops): Scan found 12 objects: 9 prod (multi-tenant but non-sensitive in this batch) and 3 staging. Listing uploaded to the incident.

toni (compliance): Even if low-sensitivity, we need incident log for auditors. Please capture timeline, affected ARNs, and whether any external principals accessed those objects.

kms-bot: Permission boundary change event: 2026-04-10T03:02Z applied to account 123456789012; impacted roles include backup-uploader. No KMS grants were created/revoked.

leah (infra-oncall): Plan: 1) Revert boundary for backup-uploader or add explicit kms:GenerateDataKey permission, 2) Recreate any missing KMS grants if required, 3) Re-upload affected snapshots with SSE-KMS, 4) Add CI test for permission boundary simulation. I'll open infra PR and revert the boundary for the backup-uploader role now.

dan (backup-service): After boundary revert, I will run re-upload job and verify `head-object` shows `x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms`. Also adding enforcement: fail upload if GenerateDataKey fails.

ravi (encops): Also recommend rotating the CMK or creating a new key for re-encrypts if we suspect keys might have been exposed; but given this was an upload-time omission and no Decrypt logs, rotation optional. Compliance: your call.

toni (compliance): For audit, we prefer re-encrypt + a short CMK rotation window for affected tenants. I'll coordinate with product owners. Please keep the incident open until re-encrypts are complete.

leah (infra-oncall): Boundary revert PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/459 (revert for backup-uploader). Pushed temporary deny on PutObject until re-upload completes.

dan (backup-service): Re-upload started. First object shows SSE header present on `head-object`. Proceeding in parallel.

kms-bot: Note: consider creating a short-lived grant for `backup-uploader` next time role changes to avoid this class of failure.
